item.title: Early Addition: Good luck docking a Citi Bike in all this
item.description: Because the docks are on the fritz, here are your early links: Queer hockey scene in NYC, Trump administration's cartoon lump of coal, long silent videos of someone walking through an English village and more. [ more › ]

item.title: Brace for 'dangerously low' wind chills, New Yorkers — and no relief until next week
item.description: A woman walks in Midtown amid piles of snow on Feb. 1, 2026. Real-feel temperatures will plunge again heading into the weekend, meteorologists say. [ more › ]

item.title: Modern NYC subway gates tested by the MTA use AI tech to track fare evaders
item.description: Fare gates designed by Cubic are currently being tested at Atlantic Terminal. A competition is underway among three private firms that are all trying to ink a massive contract to overhaul the subway's fare gates. [ more › ]

item.title: NYC Council speaker says year-round outdoor dining should return
item.description: Le Dive, a restaurant and wine bar at 37 Canal St., currently enjoys all three forms of outdoor dining: Open Streets seating (foreground), sidewalk seating (background), and a roadway dining shed (back left). Julie Menin vows to "fix" the strict regulations on businesses setting up seating on city streets. [ more › ]

item.title: NY Gov. Kathy Hochul picks Adrienne Adams as her running mate
item.description: Governor Hochul delivers remarks at the National Action Network Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Day Public Policy Forum. Hochul said the former New York City Council speaker is a fighter who would help her stand up to President Trump. [ more › ]

item.title: Months without showers: Harlem building’s residents stuck in Legionella limbo.
item.description: 3333 Broadway Legionella has been confirmed in the water supply, but not a larger outbreak. Remediation could take months or longer. [ more › ]

item.title: NYC invests in firm that helps ICE deport people. The city comptroller is concerned.
item.description: Concern over ICE enforcement in Minneapolis have raised concern in New York City about city pension fund holdings in Palantir Technologies, whose products are used in immigration enforcement. City Comptroller Mark Levine is pressing for an inquiry into Palantir Technologies, citing human rights concerns. [ more › ]

item.title: Mayor Mamdani calls AI-generated images depicting him with Jeffrey Epstein 'incredibly difficult'
item.description: Fake images depicting the mayor as a child with disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein circulated online in recent days, after the U.S. Department of Justice released its latest trove of Epstein files. [ more › ]

item.title: 911 call shows Queens family asked for ambulance before NYPD shot son in mental health crisis
item.description: A family member tries to intervene as Jabez Chakraborty approaches officers in his Queens home. A newly released 911 call shows the family asked for involuntary medical transport and told dispatchers the man was not violent or armed. [ more › ]

item.title: He helped create an NYPD unit to respond to protests. Now, he's calling for its overhaul.
item.description: Anthony Raganella, a retired NYPD deputy inspector who helped establish the SRG, in 2016. The NYPD’s Strategic Response Group has been criticized by civil liberties groups and others who have accused officers of brutality while responding to protests. [ more › ]
